title: Review: Lenses; Physics of the eye
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W13-uk1#t3 term and clue written for the game; X-EYE-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W13-uk1#t1 term and clue written for the game; X-EYE-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W13-uk1#N.3, X-EYE-1#N.6, X-EYE-2#N.7, W13-uk1#N.7, X-EYE-1#N.9, X-EYE-2#N.8, W13-uk1#N.6, X-EYE-1#N.10, X-EYE-2#N.5, X-EYE-1#N.3, X-EYE-2#N.3, X-EYE-1#N.8. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Doublet
items.clue: Two thin lenses glued in contact, often found inside a camera, whose P values simply add.

items.label: Myopia
items.clue: Eye too powerful for its length, so distant objects blur; corrected with a diverging lens.

items.label: Lens power
items.clue: Reciprocal of the focal length in metres: positive when converging, negative when diverging.

items.label: Accommodation
items.clue: Ciliary muscles change the shape of the eye lens, altering its power to focus at different distances.

questions.stem: A thin converging lens of focal length 40 cm is placed in contact with a thin diverging lens of focal length 20 cm. What is the power of the combination?
A student can read a page 20 cm away clearly, but road signs more than 3 m away look blurred. Which defect does she have, and which lens corrects it?

options.text: Hypermetropia, corrected by a converging lens
Myopia, corrected by a converging lens
Myopia, corrected by a diverging lens
Hypermetropia, corrected by a diverging lens

questions.explanation: Her far point is about 3 m, not infinity: distant light focuses in front of the retina because the eye is too powerful. A diverging lens (negative power) reduces the total power.

questions.stem: A student with normal eyesight (near point 25 cm, far point at infinity) tries on a friend's glasses of power −2.5 D. What is her range of vision through them?
questions.explanation: v = −0.25 m: 1/u = −2.5 + 4.0 = 1.5, u = 0.67 m. Distant objects give an image 0.40 m away, which she can still focus.

questions.stem: A camera lens must have a focal length of 50 mm. It is made of two thin lenses in contact. One is converging, with focal length 40 mm. What must the focal length of the other be?
A man sees distant hills clearly, but his near point is 1.2 m from his eye. He wants to read a page held 25 cm away. Which lens does he need, and what must it do?

options.text: A converging lens that forms a virtual image of the page 1.2 m from his eye
A converging lens that forms a real image of the page on his retina by itself
A diverging lens that spreads the light so the image moves back onto the retina
A converging lens that forms a virtual image of the page 25 cm from his eye

questions.explanation: His eye is too weak. The converging lens adds power and places a virtual image at his near point, which he can focus.

questions.stem: A short-sighted patient has a near point of 10 cm and a far point of 40 cm. She is given glasses of power −2.5 D. What is her range of vision while wearing them?
questions.explanation: Far: f = −0.40 m, so distant objects image at her far point. Near: v = −0.10 m, 1/u = −2.5 + 10 = 7.5, u = 0.13 m.

questions.stem: An object is 0.20 m from a thin converging lens of power +8.0 D. How far from the lens is the image?
A short-sighted woman's glasses have a power of −2.5 D. With them, she sees distant objects clearly. Where is her far point without glasses?

options.text: At infinity, like a normal eye

questions.explanation: f = 1/(−2.5) = −0.40 m. For u = ∞, v = f = −0.40 m: the lens puts distant objects at 40 cm, so that is her far point.

questions.stem: A short-sighted student's far point is 0.50 m from his eye. He wears old glasses of power −1.5 D. What is his far point while wearing them?
With age, the eye lens stiffens: the ciliary muscles can no longer make it as fat as before. How does this affect a person's vision?

options.text: Their near point moves further away; distant vision is unaffected.
Their far point moves closer; near vision is unaffected.
Both their near point and their far point move closer.
Nothing changes, because the cornea does most of the bending.

questions.explanation: Near objects need the most powerful, fattest lens. A stiff lens cannot reach that power, so the nearest focusable point moves out. Distant vision uses the thin, relaxed lens, which still works.

questions.stem: A long-sighted woman has a near point of 50 cm and a far point at infinity. She wears reading glasses of power +2.0 D. What is her range of vision while wearing them?
questions.explanation: Near: v = −0.50 m, 1/u = 2.0 + 2.0 = 4.0, u = 0.25 m. Far: image at infinity, so u = f = 1/2.0 = 0.50 m.

questions.stem: Asha's far point is 80 cm from her eye; Ben's is 2.0 m from his. Which statement about their correcting lenses is right?

options.text: Ben needs the stronger lens, because his far point is further away.
Asha needs the stronger lens: −1.25 D.
Asha needs the stronger lens: +1.25 D.
Ben needs the stronger lens: −2.0 D.

questions.explanation: f = −(far point). Asha: f = −0.80 m, P = −1.25 D. Ben: f = −2.0 m, P = −0.50 D. The closer the far point, the stronger the lens.
